name: Entry into cognition-only (vijñaptimātratā-praveśa)
method_summary: Having gathered merit and knowledge and reflected on the teachings, the bodhisattva in concentration sees objects as nothing but mental speech, rests in mind-only that appears as them, then no longer apprehends the object (the grasped is abandoned), then abandons the apprehension of mind-only itself (the grasper), and non-conceptual wisdom free of duality arises: 'where there is nothing grasped there is no grasping'.

names.name: wu weishi guan 五重唯識觀 (later Faxiang form)

stage: prayoga-mārga (the four aids to penetration) leading to darśana-mārga
prerequisites: accumulation of merit and knowledge; hearing and reflection on the Mahāyāna teaching; stable calm
signs_of_progress: objects no longer seen apart from mental speech (heat); increase of the light of Dharma (peak); abiding in mind-only (patience); only the grasper remains (supreme mundane quality); non-conceptual wisdom (first ground)

warnings.text: Even the thought 'all this is cognition-only' is an apprehension that places something before oneself; one who holds it does not yet abide in cognition-only.

name: Contemplation of the three natures
method_summary: The dependent is entered first as the absence of duality, then as mere imagination with non-existent duality, then the perfected as the being of that absence; the magical elephant is the model: seeing no elephant, the shape vanishing and the wood seen, all at once — understanding, abandonment and attainment of the three natures are simultaneous.

name: The four investigations and four exact knowledges
method_summary: Investigating names, things, designations of own-nature and designations of particulars as mere designations, and then knowing each exactly as it is; by these the bodhisattva at the stage of practice by resolve enters cognition-only.
notes: List recalled from the Mahāyānasaṃgraha and Bodhisattvabhūmi; to be checked.

name: The nine stages of settling the mind (navākārā cittasthiti)
method_summary: The mind is withdrawn from outer objects and bound to the object; settled firmly by refining it; re-settled when it strays through lapse of mindfulness; settled closely; tamed by seeing the danger in distracting signs; calmed by seeing the danger in discursive thoughts and hindrances; fully calmed by not tolerating them when they arise; made one-pointed as an uninterrupted flow with effort; and concentrated when, by repeated practice, it flows spontaneously. Six powers (hearing, reflection, mindfulness, awareness, vigour, familiarity) accomplish them; four attentions accompany them.
stage: calm abiding (śamatha), prior to the first absorption
signs_of_progress: pliancy of body and mind; spontaneous flow of concentration

warnings.text: The five faults — laziness, forgetting the instruction, sinking and agitation, non-application and over-application — obstruct the stages and must be countered by the eight formations.

name: Calm abiding (śamatha) in Yogācāra sources
method_summary: Calm is the path of gathering the names of the teachings into one; lifting the sunken mind, calming the agitated one, and leaving it in equanimity when calm; it culminates in pliancy and the basic absorption.

equivalents.note: the sūtra source of the same practice
Kamalaśīla's presentation draws on the Yogācāra nine stages and five faults

name: Insight (vipaśyanā) in Yogācāra sources
method_summary: Insight investigates the meanings of the teachings and the reflection-images of meditation: discerning, thoroughly investigating, considering and examining dharmas in their extent and reality, through the four reasonings; united with calm it is the joined path.

name: The eight antidotal formations
method_summary: Against laziness: desire-to-act, effort, faith and pliancy; against forgetting the instruction: mindfulness; against sinking and agitation: awareness that notices them; against non-application: the intention that applies the remedy; against over-application: equanimity that lets the mind flow when they have ceased.

name: The seven attentions (sapta manaskārāḥ)
method_summary: The yogin frees himself from desire for sense-pleasures by (1) discerning the coarseness of the lower and the peace of the higher level, (2) resolve, (3) seclusion (abandoning the stronger afflictions), (4) gathering delight, (5) examination (checking for remaining desire), (6) the completion of practice, (7) its fruit — the absorption.

sources.ref: fourth part of the third yogasthāna

name: Meditation objects that purify temperament
method_summary: The meditation object is prescribed by temperament: the unattractive for the lustful, loving-kindness for the hateful, dependent origination for the deluded, analysis of the elements for the proud, mindfulness of breathing for the discursive.
prerequisites: a teacher who can discern the practitioner's temperament

name: Contemplation of the unattractive
method_summary: Śrāvakabhūmi contribution: the sixfold contemplation of the unattractive (inner and outer) as the remedy for those of lustful temperament.
notes: Shared id; U41 contributes the Yogācāra (Śrāvakabhūmi) placement only.

name: The four immeasurables
method_summary: Śrāvakabhūmi contribution: loving-kindness pervading friend, enemy and neutral in all directions, prescribed for those of hating temperament; the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra's chapter on worship, service and the immeasurables.

name: Mindfulness of breathing (Śrāvakabhūmi)
method_summary: Mindfulness whose object is the in- and out-breath, prescribed for the discursive temperament; the Śrāvakabhūmi treats it in detail (including counting) and notes that it is not practised above the third absorption, where breathing ceases.

equivalents.note: the Sarvāstivāda sixfold breath practice (counting etc.)

notes: Internal details beyond the checked lines (object, temperament, limit at the third dhyāna) recalled.

name: Analysis of the elements (dhātuprabheda)
method_summary: For the proud: analysing the body into the six elements (earth, water, fire, air, space, consciousness), which dissolves the perception of the body as a solid lump.

name: The four applications of mindfulness (Yogācāra)
method_summary: Mindfulness of body, feeling, mind and dharmas, cultivated for entry into the four truths: body because of badness, feeling as the cause of craving, mind as the basis (of the self-notion), dharmas for non-delusion about defilement and purification.

name: The ten practices of the Dharma (daśa dharmacaritāni)
method_summary: Copying the teaching, worshipping it, giving it, listening to it, reading it, memorizing it, explaining it, reciting it, reflecting on it and meditating on it — an immeasurable mass of merit.

name: Hearing, reflection and cultivation
method_summary: Wisdom arises in three stages — from hearing the teaching, from reflecting on it with reasoning, and from meditative cultivation — which are three of the seventeen stages of the Yogācārabhūmi; for the pramāṇa school, reasoning (cintā) establishes what cultivation then makes vivid.

name: Taking and keeping the bodhisattva vow (Yogācāra rite)
method_summary: The vow of the threefold discipline is taken before a teacher who holds it and is learned and capable (or, lacking one, before the buddhas); the four offences equivalent to defeat and the lesser faults are avoided; a lost vow may be retaken; lesser faults are confessed.

warnings.text: An offence committed with strong affliction destroys the vow.

equivalents.note: the Yogācāra ('vast conduct') form of the bodhisattva vow, distinct from the Madhyamaka form of the Śikṣāsamuccaya

name: The four yogic stages of the Laṅkāvatāra
method_summary: Mount to mind-only and stop imagining external objects; rest in suchness and pass beyond mind-only; pass beyond the imageless (even non-dual awareness as an image); abiding in the imageless, see the Mahāyāna.

name: Cultivation of compassion over many lives
method_summary: Compassion, repeatedly cultivated, becomes the mind's nature and grows by its own momentum without limit, because mind continues across lives; perfected, it moves one to remove others' suffering and is the root of a buddha's authority.

name: Cultivation of the vision of selflessness
method_summary: Seeing selflessness is the antidote that uproots self-love and its faults; cultivated long, in many ways, it makes virtues and faults clear and removes the imprints; liberation comes from seeing emptiness.

name: Meditative cultivation of a real object (to yogic perception)
method_summary: A real object (above all the four truths) is cultivated until, at its culmination, it appears vividly and without conceptual construction — yogic perception.

warnings.text: Vividness alone does not make a cognition valid: those overcome by desire, grief, fear, madness or dream also see unreal things as if before them.

name: Monastic debate on valid cognition (bsdus grwa / rtsod pa)
method_summary: The Tibetan monastic training in epistemology through formal debate: a defender answers a challenger's consequences about definitions, divisions and pervasions, beginning with the Collected Topics and proceeding to the Pramāṇavārttika.

equivalents.note: the Nyāya practice of debate; both aim at truth and codify defeat
